title: The Static of New Lagos
premise: Yara Nystrom, a cargo hauler who spent twelve years staying invisible in the contested orbits of New Lagos, intercepts a distress beacon broadcasting in Old Meridian—a language extinct since the First Collapse. The signal is a dead-man's switch from a peace faction believed destroyed, containing proof that the war's opening attack was staged by the colonial government itself. Hunted by both fleets and shadowed by his estranged lover, fleet intelligence officer Sefu Adeyemi, Yara must choose between delivering the truth and protecting the people who once abandoned him. He broadcasts the evidence at the cost of his ship and nearly his life, ending the war but forcing both sides—and Sefu—to reckon with what survival was built upon.
about_author: Coral Ashgrove is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who traded port audits for orbital fiction. They write stories about ordinary people trapped between institutions and their consciences.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Establishes his careful, invisible life hauling freight through contested orbits and the routines that keep him off both fleets' radar. A routine salvage contract goes wrong when his rig snags a derelict transmitting in Old Meridian—a language dead for two centuries. Emotional beat: unease beneath practiced calm, the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Switch
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He decrypts the derelict's core and finds a recorded testimony: proof the war's opening attack was staged by the colonial government. The recorder names him—his mother was among the peace faction's founders. Emotional beat: vertigo, as the past he buried becomes the most dangerous cargo in the system.

chapters.title: Sefu
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Fleet intelligence officer Sefu Adeyemi is ordered to find the signal's source—and realizes the derelict's last logged docking was Yara's ship. Flashbacks to their severed romance and the faction's collapse that made them both choose survival over each other. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a noose around old love.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara seeks his old smuggler contact Mama Ijeoma to decode the testimony's coordinates, paying with the last of his savings. She warns him both fleets already know the signal exists. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—he must decide who, if anyone, he can trust with the truth.

chapters.title: The Net Closes
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Sefu traces Yara to Ijeoma's station but delays her report, buying him hours and damning herself. Her superior, Commander Vasquez, grows suspicious and dispatches a strike team. Emotional beat: Sefu's quiet betrayal of her uniform, love rekindling into complicity.

chapters.title: Burn Run
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara escapes the station under fire, Ijeoma staying behind to cover him and paying with her freedom. A brutal chase through the Kessler shoals leaves his ship crippled and his AI, BRIGHT, sacrificing itself to mask his signature. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal, grief in the dark.

chapters.title: What the War Was Built On
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Sefu confronts Vasquez, learns the government knew the attack was staged all along, and is offered a promotion to stay silent. She reads the intercepted testimony and recognizes her own father's voice among the conspirators. Emotional beat: shattering—the war she served was a lie with her family's fingerprints on it.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Tower
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara reaches the derelict's coordinates: an ancient peace-faction relay above New Lagos, half-functional and guarded by a dying caretaker AI holding his mother's final message to him. Both fleets converge. Emotional beat: tenderness and resolve—he hears her voice, and chooses the truth over the escape she'd want for him.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. As the fleets exchange fire around the relay, Sefu defects mid-battle, clearing Yara's transmission window at gunpoint against Vasquez. Yara broadcasts the testimony system-wide, his ship burning around him. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved—Sefu chooses him and the truth, both nearly dying for it.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet After
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV, epilogue. Ceasefire holds; tribunals begin, and Vasquez faces charges. Yara, scarred and shipless, and Sefu, stripped of rank, drift to a rebuilt station where Ijeoma waits, freed in the armistice. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—truth cost everything, but for the first time in twelve years, Yara is visible, and unafraid.
